question: Quantisation error of an 8-bit A/D converter for an analog voltage in the range −1 to +1 volt is approximately equal to ____ mv
solution:
The correct answer is __2**(2 mV)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The quantisation error is the difference between the actual analog value and its digital representation.
 
• For an 8-bit A/D converter, the total number of quantization levels is given by 2⁸ = 256.
 
• The range of the given analog input is -1 to +1 volts, which is a total range of 2 volts.
 
• Thus, the resolution of the A/D converter is frac{{Total Range}}{{Number of Levels}} = (2)/(256) = 0.0078125 { volts or } 7.8125 { mV} .
 
• The quantisation error is half of the resolution, which is approximately (7.8125)/(2) = 3.90625 { mV} .
 
• When considering approximate values, the quantisation error is closest to 2 mV.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Concepts:**
 
 
• Quantisation error decreases as the resolution (number of bits) of the A/D converter increases.
 
• Higher bit A/D converters provide better accuracy and finer measurements.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Used in digital signal processing, audio, video, and other electronic systems.
 
• Critical in precise measurement devices such as oscilloscopes and medical instruments.
